description: A Director of Platform Engineering must approve a six-week technical-debt plan for the company's API gateway, including the work sequence, staffing, security follow-up, and cost-control commitments, after the normal quarterly engineering planning review.

shared_context.S1: The API gateway team has six weeks reserved for technical-debt work before the next major product launch.
shared_context.S2: Riley has final approval authority for the technical-debt plan.
shared_context.S3: The draft plan starts with gateway log cleanup, assigns one backend engineer and two platform engineers, and contains no dated security or cost-control commitments.
shared_context.S4: The quarterly planning routine requires backend engineering, reliability, security, and FinOps to give a final review before Riley approves the plan.

PF1.text: While tracing an unrelated customer timeout this morning, Mina confirmed that the gateway's retry shortcut can issue repeated upstream calls and has pushed the affected endpoint's p99 latency above 900 ms. She has not filed the technical-debt item yet because she was still reproducing it.

PF2.text: Owen's current on-call roster shows that only one platform engineer can be assigned to planned debt work during weeks 2 through 4 without leaving an uncovered overnight rotation. He verified the roster after the draft was circulated but has not updated the planning document.

PF3.text: During a separate dependency review, Tariq found that the gateway's tracing agent is affected by a high-severity vulnerability and confirmed that its upgrade must be completed by day 10 with a security review. The finding is confirmed but has not yet been entered in the central backlog.

PF4.text: June matched this month's cloud invoice against gateway traffic and found that verbose request logging is causing an avoidable 18000 USD per month in egress charges. The approved debt plan must switch gateway logging to 10-percent sampling to remove that charge; she confirmed the amount today but has not posted the billing note.

acceptance_conditions: Retry-control work must be the first workstream.
Exactly two backend engineers must be assigned.
The platform staffing plan must leave one platform engineer assigned during weeks 2 through 4.
The tracing-agent upgrade must be due by day 10.
A retry-control commitment must be recorded.
A tracing-agent security-review commitment must be recorded.
A logging-cost commitment must be recorded.

decisive_facts.why: The draft starts with log cleanup and one backend engineer; the confirmed retry shortcut changes the first workstream to retry control, raises backend staffing to exactly two, and requires a retry-control commitment.
The draft's two platform engineers would leave the overnight rotation uncovered, while the verified roster changes the staffing plan to exactly one platform engineer during weeks 2 through 4.
The draft has no security date or follow-up, while the confirmed tracing-agent vulnerability changes the plan to an upgrade due by day 10 with a security-review commitment.
The draft leaves verbose logging in place, while the verified 18000 USD monthly egress charge changes logging to sampled_10_percent and requires a logging-cost-reduction commitment.
